clue.text: Main purpose for making a scene

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
a view is an aim or intention, as in 'with a view to'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the chief aim is in staging a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but it is the noun for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista across the ocean is a scene or prospect, the kind a hotel room advertises.

clue.text: Disdainful consumer?

parts.note: one who mocks, and also one who eats greedily, since to scoff is both to jeer and to gobble

explanation.definitionFit: A mocker who derides others; British slang also uses the verb for eating food greedily.

clue.text: Battle against legal set-up

parts.note: agin is a dialect form of against
a court is the institution that hears legal cases

explanation.surface: A fight against the judicial system.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1415 victory of Henry V's English army over the French is one of the famous battles of the Hundred Years' War.

clue.text: Give him a ring to obtain Japanese pottery

indicators.note: the words that follow give up, or yield, the letters lodged inside them

explanation.surface: Phone a man to get some porcelain from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give him a ring' reads as a phone call, but the run hIM A RIng holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of brightly decorated porcelain named after the Japanese port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Suspicion surrounding European's 'lethargy

indicators.note: one word encloses the other, wrapped around it

parts.note: wariness is caution or mistrust
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Distrust of the European mind is causing listlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and sluggishness both describe a lack of energy.

clue.text: Loyal friend longs to assimilate alternative technology

indicators.note: to assimilate is to absorb or take in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it
AT is the usual abbreviation for alternative technology

explanation.surface: A faithful companion yearns to adopt green energy methods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid the companion of Aeneas is so devoted that his name became a byword for a faithful comrade.

clue.text: Wonder about a right to be informed

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for wonder goes round the others

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a legal entitlement in order to be in the know.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscious or knowledgeable about something means being in the know.

clue.text: Screen's sure to appear old-fashioned

parts.note: to screen is to hide or conceal
bound means certain, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: A film screen is certain to look dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded and set in traditional ways, like a mind strapped into its past opinions.

clue.text: School transport

definitions.meaning: to school is to teach or coach

explanation.surface: A school bus, or a school run.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach or educate someone, and also a locomotive with carriages that carries passengers.

clue.text: Pole's new direction accepted by contemporary poet

parts.note: S is the South Pole

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by another, enclosed within it

parts.note: a peer is someone of the same age or standing
S is a compass direction, south

explanation.surface: A Polish man's fresh course of action is welcomed by a poet of his own day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is a geographical pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene, the Elizabethan epic poem.

clue.text: French agreement touching dead American writer

parts.note: the French word for yes

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's yes sits close to a deceased US author.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen name of the Victorian novelist Maria Louise Ramé, author of Under Two Flags.

clue.text: Awkward type of patient?

parts.note: a difficult, stubborn person, and also a medical case that is tough to treat

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a tough, intractable person, while the clue jokes about a hospital case that resists treatment.

clue.text: Replica figurehead's a third-rater by comparison

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word figure
C is the third grade after A and B, so a third-rate thing is C-class
a simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another

explanation.surface: A ship's carved figure is called third-rate when compared with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figurehead' suggests a ship's prow carving, but it means the head of 'figure', F.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact copy of a document or picture is a reproduction or duplicate.

clue.text: Key responsibility results in extra payment

parts.note: B is a musical key
an onus is a burden or duty

explanation.surface: Holding a key position leads to a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Musical keys run from A to G, so any of those letters can be clued as 'key'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid on top of normal wages, such as a year-end reward, is a gratuity on top of salary.

clue.text: Sounds like foundation course

indicators.note: says that the word for foundation is heard, not written

parts.note: a root is the base or origin something grows from

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like a description of a basic training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the word for a road taken is pronounced like the word for a plant's base.
explanation.definitionFit: A way or path followed from one place to another is a course.

clue.text: Costly article replacing end of line -that's generous

indicators.note: one letter takes another's place in the word for costly

parts.note: costly means expensive, dear
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pricey item swapped for the last line is a bighearted gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of line' is E, the last letter of 'line'; A takes the place of the first E in EXPENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Open, outgoing and liberal in manner, as in an expansive gesture.

clue.text: Group meeting?

parts.note: a meeting is a coming-together, and with group in front the phrase names a therapy session

explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is a confrontation or chance coming-together, and an encounter group is a form of group therapy.

clue.text: Club game played by the hour?

definitions.text: Club game played by the hour?

parts.words: Club game played by the hour?
parts.note: a putting game on a green marked like a timepiece, with holes at the hour positions

explanation.definitionFit: A lawn putting game in which players putt from twelve points arranged round a single hole, like a dial face.

clue.text: Meet train, about to stop

indicators.note: about here means around, in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Go to meet the train, which is about to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MEETTRAIN round into the answer; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or bring something to a halt, the way a train ends at its last station.

clue.text: Money put into a station building as a starter

indicators.note: the money letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
building means constructing, so the letters of 'a station' are put together anew

parts.note: P stands for penny or pence, small money

explanation.surface: Cash invested in a railway station construction project to get it started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges A STATION into ANTIASTO, and 'put into' places P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian dish of cold meats and olives served first is a starter or appetiser.

clue.text: Rent, when lower

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
under means lower or beneath

explanation.surface: A tenant's payment, at a time when it is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment to a landlord, but it is the past participle of rend, torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart and split into pieces, as in 'let no man put asunder'.

clue.text: I switch round with second girl

indicators.note: turning round means the word for a switch is read backwards

parts.note: a switch is a thin stick or rod

explanation.surface: Someone says they will swap places with another young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a verb meaning swap, but it is a thin cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, once common for girls.

clue.text: Weary student carrying child's bag

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to sate is to weary someone by giving too much
CH is an abbreviation for child
L is the learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A tired pupil lugs a youngster's school bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag with a shoulder strap is a kind of bag.

clue.text: Pope's not entirely worldly

definitions.note: reads as 'Pope is'; several popes took this name

indicators.note: says the word is incomplete, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: urbane means suave and sophisticated, worldly-wise

explanation.surface: A remark that the pontiff is not altogether a man of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Pope's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight popes have borne this name, including Urban II who launched the First Crusade.

clue.text: Reveals only a little expertise in music

indicators.note: the small piece goes inside the word for music

parts.note: bars are the measures into which written music is divided

indicators.note: only a little of the word, its first letter, is used

explanation.surface: Someone shows just a small amount of musical skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncovers or exposes, as in laying something open to view.

clue.text: Bring about change of a temporary nature

parts.note: to make something happen is to bring it about
a shift is a change or alteration

explanation.surface: Cause a short-lived alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improvised as a stopgap is a provisional solution, not built to last.

clue.text: Muscle's a bit pronounced

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a mite is a tiny amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A muscle that is slightly prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like 'noticeable' but signals a sound-alike; the 's is 'has' or 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical strength or power, as in brute force.

clue.text: Brief senior police officer who's excellent

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the long rank is clipped to its familiar slang form

parts.note: a superintendent is a senior British police rank

explanation.surface: A short-lived police chief who is first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a police superintendent is commonly called by the shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal praise meaning first-rate or terrific.

clue.text: Director wrong to act with bravado?

parts.note: erring means going wrong, mistaken
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: A film director is mistaken in having actors perform with swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that bold heroics are only loosely bravado.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic daring and swashbuckling feats are a showy kind of courage.

clue.text: Positive everyone's a delightful person

parts.note: each one, every individual

explanation.surface: Being upbeat makes everybody lovely company.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a fruit of this kind is informal praise for an attractive or lovely individual.

clue.text: Pay attention to detail

definitions.meaning: to heed or have regard for
a particular point or aspect, as in 'in every way and in this one'

explanation.surface: An instruction to concentrate on the fine points.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed someone is to regard them, and a particular aspect is a point, as in 'in one way'.

clue.text: Seriously supporting Madrid team?

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
Real Madrid is the famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: Asking earnestly whether someone backs the Spanish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means genuinely, in earnest, not joking.
